question: Should Phase 1 permanently allow owner-controlled agents to mutate global session groups, cancel any task inside their session tree, and trigger automatic rollback of their own model selection under the proposed failure rules?
rationale: These are intentional expansions of agent authority and persisted session/provider behavior; source-level correctness cannot determine whether the proposed global, tree-scoped, and automatic boundaries match maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Approve with refreshed proof
options.body: Keep the proposed authority model, resolve the stacked conflict, and require exact-head live proof for global groups, tree cancellation, visible-worktree cleanup, and model rollback before landing.

options.title: Narrow mutation authority
options.body: Limit group operations or cancellation to a smaller session-owned scope and require explicit user action for model recovery before merging.

options.title: Split the phase
options.body: Land read-only status and ledger visibility separately while holding global mutations, cancellation, visible worktrees, and rollback for narrower follow-up reviews.

recommendation.title: Approve with refreshed proof
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed authority model, resolve the stacked conflict, and require exact-head live proof for global groups, tree cancellation, visible-worktree cleanup, and model rollback before landing.
